register.level: tradesman's speech (a hat-seller) that is rude and needling at his own table and grovelling in court
register.summary: At the tea-table he makes personal remarks, asks riddles with no answers, and turns Alice's words into pedantic word-games. Everything he says circles back to time and tea (per SUP-012, Time exists only in his talk and a stopped watch, and he speaks of Time as 'him'). In the witness box the needling collapses into a whining refrain, 'I'm a poor man, your Majesty', and his grammar slips ('I can't go no lower').

examples.text: Your hair wants cutting,
If you knew Time as well as I do, you wouldn't talk about wasting it. It's him.
I'm a poor man, your Majesty, —and I hadn't begun my tea—not above a week or so—and what with the bread-and-butter getting so thin—and the twinkling of the tea—

catchphrases.text: Why is a raven like a writing-desk?
I'm a poor man, your Majesty
tea / tea-time / It's always six o'clock now

sentence_style.length: short jabs (median 9 words) at the table; one long fanciful explanation (Time and the clock); breathless dash-chained babble in court (mean 12.9)

patterns.rule: Personal remarks and put-downs aimed at Alice, often as a short conditional rebuke.

examples.text: Your hair wants cutting,
Then you shouldn't talk,
… so I should think you could draw treacle out of a treacle-well—eh, stupid?

patterns.rule: Pedantic inversion and hair-splitting on word meanings ('Not the same thing a bit!', 'it's very easy to take more than nothing').

examples.text: Not the same thing a bit! You might just as well say that 'I see what I eat' is the same thing as 'I eat what I see'!
You mean you can't take less, it's very easy to take more than nothing.
Why should it? Does your watch tell you what year it is?

patterns.rule: Time, tea and the watch as his fixed topic; Time personified as 'him'.

examples.text: Two days wrong! I told you butter wouldn't suit the works!
And ever since that, he won't do a thing I ask! It's always six o'clock now.
I want a clean cup, let's all move one place on.

patterns.rule: Riddles and questions he has no intention of answering.

examples.text: Have you guessed the riddle yet?
I haven't the slightest idea,

patterns.rule: In court: whining self-pity, blame-shifting to the March Hare and Dormouse, and slipping grammar.

examples.text: Well, at any rate, the Dormouse said—
I can't go no lower, I'm on the floor, as it is.
I keep them to sell, I've none of my own. I'm a hatter.

preferred_fields: time-telling and the calendar (day of the month, March, six o'clock, half-past one)

examples.text: What day of the month is it?
Yes, but some crumbs must have got in as well, you shouldn't have put it in with the bread-knife.

address.self: I; 'we' for the tea-party ('we've no time to wash the things')
address.to_the_king: your Majesty / I beg pardon, your Majesty

examples.text: I beg pardon, your Majesty, for bringing these in: but I hadn't quite finished my tea when I was sent for.
He won't stand beating. Now, if you only kept on good terms with him, he'd do almost anything you liked with the clock.

forbidden_words.reason: he is never polite at his own table: no please/thank-you in 43 spoken lines; his only courtesy ('I beg pardon, your Majesty') is fear-driven and aimed at the King

forbidden_words.domain: the Queen's death formula as his own order
forbidden_words.reason: he quotes the Queen's 'Off with his head!' only inside reported speech (ch007-d0057); he never commands it

drift.change: Tea-party host: rude, needling, pedantic, in control of the conversation.
Witness box: the swagger collapses; self-pity refrain, stammering dash-chains, blame-shifting and ungrammatical double negatives.

recitation_repertoire.note: 'Twinkle, twinkle, little bat!' (ch007-d0051, ch007-d0055) is sung text, excluded from the hit-rate denominator.

backtest_markers.regex: \b(your hair|personal remarks|stupid|you shouldn't|then you shouldn't|of course you don't|it is the same thing with you|be quick about it)\b
\b(poor man|hatter|none of my own|isn't mine|can't remember|go no lower|beg pardon)\b|^you did!
^(not the same|not I|not at first|why should it|exactly so|yes, but|which is just|yes, that's it|you mean)\b|\b(take (less|more)|same thing)\b

backtest_markers.rule_ref: vocabulary: fellow tea-party members as reference points

backtest.method: marker-claim back-test: a spoken source line hits when it matches >=1 backtest_markers regex and no forbidden_words regex; verse (recited text) excluded; full definition runs/p3-dialogue-style-pb1/result.json#backtest_method
